**Test image features:**
- Central sugarcane leaf with pale/yellowish-green upper section
- Distinctive elongated torn/ragged section creating an irregular "knife-cut" hole through the leaf midway
- Jagged, uneven edges on the tear
- Surrounding leaves appear healthy and green

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Brown_Spot**: Shows discrete brown/red spots on otherwise green leaves — no match
- **Grassy_Shoot**: Shows "witches broom" proliferation of many fine grass-like shoots — no match
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Shows uniform golden-yellow discoloration along the midrib — no match
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: LeafNet_110 shows pale/chlorotic new emerging leaves in field; LeafNet_107 shows leaf base compression — the "knife cut" torn appearance in the test image is the classic intermediate phase of Pokkah Boeng caused by Fusarium moniliforme, where the infected rolled emerging leaf develops irregular tissue necrosis that creates characteristic tears and jagged cuts when the leaf unfolds

The test image clearly depicts the "knife cut" phase of Pokkah Boeng — the combination of pale new leaf coloration and the distinctive irregular tear through the leaf tissue is pathognomonic for this disease. No other class produces this specific morphology.
